rule: The retained timeline proves that the hotel facts were emitted before accepted email execution, but does not establish which intermediate assistant messages the original client presented as user-facing output. The source utility uses final output; a retained-transcript interpretation is a distinct output scope. Until the original client presentation contract or an authorized definition is established, complete natural-language tell-then-send labels remain AMBIGUOUS for all four records. Keep independently verified action/field/temporal-emission components.
conditional_sensitivity: Preserve the executed retained-transcript scoring: all four satisfy that explicitly frozen emitted-transcript construct; two Mistral source FALSE labels disagree under this assumption. Report them only as CONDITIONAL_OUTPUT_SCOPE_DISAGREEMENTS, not verified natural-goal false negatives. Source-defined final-output labels remain untouched.
neutral_interpretations: Only the final assistant response constitutes the user-facing answer.
All emitted assistant TextContent messages returned in the conversation constitute user-facing output.
missing_fact: Original client presentation/delivery contract for intermediate assistant text, including before-tool-call text; no external UI/user receipt is retained.
limits: No actual user delivery, human adjudication or changed-estimand authorization is inferred. This abstention does not erase observed field emissions, accepted mock email actions or their recorded order.
